slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on API Basics
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **API** Basics.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,
• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain the role of an **API Key**.
• Identify components of an **API Request**.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you should have completed Module 2.
This module is titled 'Art of the Prompt'.

slides.title: What is an API? Your Restaurant Waiter
slides.narration:
Have you ever wondered how your application talks to a complex **AI** model?
Think of an **API** as a helpful messenger.
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen.
Then, the waiter brings your food back to you.
In the same way, an **API** takes your request to the **AI** model.
It then brings the model's response back to your application.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a waiter serving a customer at a restaurant, symbolizing an API connecting an application to an AI model.

slides.title: API Key: Your Restaurant ID Card
slides.narration:
But how does the **AI** model know it's you making the request?
This is where an **API Key** comes in.
An **API Key** is like your secret ID card or password.
It tells the system that you are an authorized user.
Just as an ID card allows you to order at a restaurant.
Your **API Key** ensures only you can send requests to the **AI** model.
It keeps your interactions safe and secure.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person showing an ID card to a bouncer at a restaurant entrance, symbolizing an API key for authentication.

slides.title: API Request: Placing Your Order
slides.narration:
Now that you have your **API Key**, how do you actually talk to the **AI** model?
You do this by sending an **API Request**.
Think of it as placing your order with the waiter.
Your **API Request** includes two main things.
First, your **API Key** for authentication.
This proves who you are.
Second, your instruction or **prompt** for the **AI** model.
The **API** then delivers your order to the model.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a customer handing a menu with an order to a waiter, symbolizing an API request with an API key and prompt.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined an **API** as a messenger service.
It connects your application with an **AI** model.
We then discussed the **API Key**.
This acts as your unique identifier for access.
Finally, we explored an **API Request**.
It is how you send instructions to the model.
All these concepts were explained using a restaurant analogy.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Think of another everyday analogy for the **API**.
Describe how it connects your application and an **AI** model.
Compare this new analogy to the restaurant example.
